title: Scientific replication
instructions: Listen and select the words in the transcript that differ from the audio. Select a word again to remove it.
audioText: Repeating a scientific study is sometimes treated as a straightforward test of whether the original researchers were correct. In practice, replication requires careful attention to the conditions under which a finding was produced. Differences in equipment, participants or measurement procedures can influence the result without implying misconduct. Researchers should make these differences explicit and distinguish a failure to reproduce an effect from evidence that the effect is impossible. A useful replication may reveal that an apparent general principle depends on a narrower set of circumstances. This discovery can refine a theory rather than simply discredit it. Open methods and accessible data allow others to examine competing explanations, while several independent investigations provide a stronger basis for judgement than a single dramatic success or failure reported in isolation.
passage: Repeating a scientific study is sometimes treated as a straightforward test of whether the original researchers were correct. In practice, replication requires casual attention to the conditions under which a finding was produced. Differences in equipment, participants or measurement procedures can guarantee the result without implying misconduct. Researchers should make these differences implicit and distinguish a failure to reproduce an effect from evidence that the effect is impossible. A useful replication may reveal that an apparent general principle depends on a broader set of circumstances. This discovery can abandon a theory rather than simply discredit it. Open methods and accessible data allow others to examine competing explanations, while several dependent investigations provide a stronger basis for judgement than a single dramatic success or failure reported in isolation.

corrections.explanation: Replication needs close attention to the original conditions.
Procedural differences can affect a result without guaranteeing it.
Researchers should clearly state differences between studies.
The finding may apply to fewer circumstances than expected.
A replication can improve an existing theory.
